semantic_correction.stem: A client with a healing pressure injury asks why the dietitian emphasized adequate protein intake. Which explanation is best?

options.A: Protein should be reduced during pressure-injury healing because protein breakdown creates metabolic waste that interferes with formation of new tissue.
options.B: Local wound care determines healing, so protein and overall nutritional intake have little influence once pressure offloading and dressings are started.
options.C: Vitamin and mineral supplements can substitute for adequate calories and protein during healing when the wound is receiving appropriate local treatment.
options.D: Adequate protein and overall nutrition support tissue repair and wound healing, with the nutrition plan individualized to the client's condition and intake needs.

semantic_correction.rationale: D is correct. The current 2026 StatPearls chapter on Pressure Injury states that prevention and management include adequate hydration and nutrition and that successful wound healing requires adequate nutrition. Its patient-education section states that diets for people with pressure injuries should include adequate amounts of protein, vitamins, and minerals. It also notes that chronic draining wounds can contribute to protein loss and malnutrition, supporting attention to nutritional adequacy rather than routine protein restriction. Therefore the nurse should explain that adequate protein and overall nutrition support tissue repair and healing, while the exact nutrition plan should be individualized to the client's clinical condition and intake needs. A is incorrect because routine protein restriction contradicts the source's recommendation for adequate protein. B is incorrect because nutrition is an established component of pressure-injury prevention and healing in addition to local wound care and offloading. C is incorrect because supplements do not replace adequate overall nutritional intake.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Explain that adequate individualized protein and overall nutrition support tissue repair and pressure-injury healing rather than replacing nutrition with supplements or routinely restricting protein.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: replaced the archived StatPearls source with the current Pressure Injury chapter updated July 5, 2026, removed the absolute-word and answer-length cues, rebuilt all four nutrition explanations to comparable structure, and preserved adequate individualized nutrition as the single best response.

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item tests the nutritional role of protein in pressure-injury healing with one clearly best response, balanced alternatives, and a current non-archived source.

option_audit.A: Incorrect. Current pressure-injury guidance supports adequate protein rather than routine restriction during healing.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Nutrition is a recognized component of pressure-injury prevention and healing alongside local wound care and offloading.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Vitamin or mineral supplements cannot substitute for adequate overall calories and protein when nutritional intake is insufficient.
option_audit.D: Correct. It accurately states the role of adequate protein and overall nutrition while preserving individualized care.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. D uniquely reflects current pressure-injury guidance; A restricts needed protein, B dismisses nutrition, and C substitutes supplements for adequate intake.
cueing_check: All four options are parallel nutrition explanations of comparable length and specificity; the prior 'all' distractor and uniquely-long correct response were removed.
